public_rationale: The evidence supports part of the forecast: GitHub attributed changes to inference-cost pressure and implemented usage-based billing. Reporting also shows enterprise cost controls. But these records do not complete the causal link to established enterprises rejecting the affected purchases as uneconomic. The partial evidence therefore does not meet the early-resolution rule, and the forecast has no deadline.
limitations: Support for intermediate steps is not support for the complete forecast.
The cost explanation relies on attributable news reporting because the primary announcement's body was unavailable through read_page.
Enterprise contract prices and purchase decisions are often private.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI's burn rate will eventually force price increases or onerous pricing that even well-funded enterprise customers cannot justify.

statement.excerpt: At some point, the incredible, toxic burn-rate of generative AI is going to catch up with them, which in turn will lead to price increases, or companies releasing new products and features with wildly onerous rates — like the egregious $2-a-conversation rate for Salesforce’s “Agentforce” product — that will make even stalwart enterprise customers with budget to burn unable to justify the expense.

from_speaker: or companies releasing new products and features with wildly onerous rates
even stalwart enterprise customers with budget to burn
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading predicts that provider cost pressure forces pricing changes that make affected AI purchases uneconomic even for established, well-funded enterprise customers.
The forecast requires the causal chain from provider costs through pricing to enterprise purchasing decisions.
An increased bill caused solely by greater usage is insufficient.
The Agentforce price is an existing illustration, not a future threshold or the only product covered.
This is a qualitative pricing-and-demand forecast, not a specified company revenue, loss, or spending figure.
criteria.support_condition: Provider records connect unsustainable costs to increased effective prices or onerous new pricing, and established enterprise customers subsequently reject or materially curtail the affected purchases because their value no longer justifies those prices.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive, adequately documented resolution of the alleged cost-pressure episode establishes sustainable pricing and continued economic value for the affected enterprise purchases. Temporary price reductions alone cannot disprove an indefinite forecast.

evidence.explanation: This supports the provider-cost-pressure part of the forecast. The primary announcement was not substantively readable, so this attributable report is used; it does not establish enterprise rejection.

evidence.locator: Section 'Usage-based billing is active for all Copilot plans'
evidence.explanation: This confirms implementation of the pricing-model change. Its effect on individual enterprise bills and purchasing decisions requires additional evidence.

evidence.excerpt: More recently, Microsoft updated internal guidance this August specifically to curb AI token spend.
evidence.explanation: A major enterprise reportedly imposed cost controls. That does not establish rejection of a particular purchase because provider burn forced its price higher.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Provider cost and pricing records paired with attributable decisions by established enterprises to reject or materially curtail the affected purchases because the new prices cannot be justified.
